text:
Noah: quick follow-up to the format RFC. i've been prototyping a lightweight descriptor-normalizer that annotates safetensors / legacy tarballs / multi-shard manifests into a single StreamDescriptor blob so loaders can rely on one contract. wanted to surface tradeoffs.
Asha: sounds useful. does it preserve mmap offsets / zero-copy pointers?
Noah: yes, it only annotates offsets[] when available. it must not rewrite blobs to keep mmap cheap.
Ravi: how do we carry warmup signals? scheduler needs them for prefill ordering.
Noah: normalizer emits warmupHint {mode, weight}. mode is an enum (index-first, bulk-read, layered), weight is advisory 0-1. loaders may ignore weight but must honor mode when correctness depends on it.
Asha: fallback semantics? if verify fails, should the descriptor include mirrors or a fail-hard flag?
Noah: descriptor includes alternates[] with reasons and a suggested routing policy. runtime decides whether to try alternates.
ci-bot: heads-up: please include schema_version and supported_versions in descriptor. schema-lint will fail otherwise.
Noah: will add schema_version and supported_versions. plan is: compute heavy parsing at ingest, cache descriptor in registry, do cheap verification on load. feature-flag rollout and canary on dedicated first.
Ravi: add quant_profile to the descriptor too, kernel selection depends on it.
Noah: noted. test checklist: safetensors header parse, tarball manifest index, mmap offset preservation, alternates resolution, quant_profile propagation. i'll file a mini-rfc with JSON schema and e2e plan.
Asha: :+1: add a debug endpoint to dump the resolved descriptor for model ids.
Noah: good call; adding debug-dump. filing in 20m.
